gloss: divide in two, halve; half, middle
summary: To divide, above all into two: Jacob divides his people into two camps, Gideon his men into three companies, owners divide the price of an ox, Moses the spoil between the army and the congregation; in the niphal the Jordan's waters are divided “here and here”, and a kingdom is divided. Its nouns are the half that results and the middle where the line falls: חֲצִי “half” (half a cubit, the half tribe of Manasseh, “up to half the kingdom”) and “middle” (בַּחֲצִי הַלַּיְלָה, midnight), מַחֲצִית the half shekel and midday, חָצוֹת midnight, מֶחֱצָה the half of the spoil. Akkadian eṣû “slit” and Punic ḥṣy “half” share the meaning; the rare חֵצִי “arrow” has cognates of its own (Ugaritic ḥẓ, Arabic ḥaẓwa) and its tie to the root is not clear.

words.summary: About 125 times: the half of a measure, a people, a land, a kingdom or a lifetime, and the middle of the night, the sky or a span. The brief counts 1Sa 20:36–37 and 2Ki 9:24 here as well as under the arrow חֵצִי, which shares the consonants.

senses.definition: One of two equal parts of anything: a measure, the blood of a sacrifice, a beard, a tribe, a people, a city, a kingdom.

evidence.note: “Divide the living child in two (לִשְׁנָיִם), and give הַחֲצִי to one and הַחֲצִי to the other.”
Moses took חֲצִי הַדָּם and put it in basins, and וַחֲצִי הַדָּם he threw on the altar.
“The people of Israel were divided (יֵחָלֵק): חֲצִי הָעָם followed Tibni … and הַחֲצִי followed Omri.”
The ark two cubits וָחֵצִי long, a cubit וָחֵצִי wide: the half cubit.
Half a hin of oil.
Hanun shaved off חֲצִי זְקָנָם, half their beards, and cut their garments in the middle.
“To half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph”: the half tribe east of the Jordan.
“What is your request? עַד־חֲצִי הַמַּלְכוּת, it shall be given you.” Also Est 5:6; 7:2.
The queen of Sheba: “behold, הַחֵצִי was not told me”: not even half.
The wall joined together up to its half (height).
“And half of the city shall go out into exile, and the rest of the people shall not be cut off from the city.”
Living waters go out from Jerusalem, half to the eastern sea and half to the western sea.
“For a set time, set times וָחֵצִי”: and a half, quoted in Rev 12:14.
“A time, and times, and half a time (ἥμισυ καιροῦ)”, from Dan 12:7.
Herod's oath, “up to half of my kingdom (ἕως ἡμίσους τῆς βασιλείας μου)”, in the words of Est 5:3.

senses.definition: The point that halves a span: the middle of the night, of the sky, of a lifetime, of a week of years.

evidence.note: “It was at חֲצִי הַלַּיְלָה, and Yahweh struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt”, as foretold “about חֲצֹת לַיְלָה” (Exo 11:4).
Samson lay till midnight, and rose בַּחֲצִי הַלַּיְלָה.
The sun stood still בַּחֲצִי הַשָּׁמַיִם, in the middle of the sky, and did not hasten to go down.
“Do not take me up בַּחֲצִי יָמָי; your years are through all generations”: halfway through a life, set against God's years.
Wealth gained unjustly leaves him בַּחֲצִי יָמָיו, and at his end he is a fool.
“In the half of the week (וַחֲצִי הַשָּׁבוּעַ) he shall cause sacrifice and offering to cease.”
The Mount of Olives is split מֵחֶצְיוֹ, from its middle, east and west, and חֲצִי הָהָר moves north and חֶצְיוֹ south.

evidence.locator: Est.5.3, 7.2, עַד־חֲצִי הַמַּלְכוּת → ἕως τοῦ ἡμίσους τῆς βασιλείας; Dan.12.7, וָחֵצִי → ἥμισυ; Zec.14.4 → ἥμισυ; ἥμισυ renders חֲצִי ×77

evidence.note: Herod's oath to Herodias's daughter, “whatever you ask … up to half of my kingdom”: the king's words to Esther.
“A time, and times, and half a time”: Dan 12:7's וָחֵצִי.

words.gloss: divide (in two, into parts), halve; (niphal) be divided
words.summary: Fifteen times, in the qal and niphal. To part a whole: a company into camps or bands, a price or a spoil into shares, waters to either side, a kingdom into two or four. The opposite is one: “one nation … and they shall no longer be divided into two kingdoms” (Ezk 37:22).

stems.gloss: divide, divide into parts; share out; halve; reach to the middle

senses.definition: To part a company of people or flocks into two or more groups.

evidence.note: Jacob, afraid, וַיַּחַץ the people with him, and the flocks and herds and camels, לִשְׁנֵי מַחֲנוֹת, into two camps.
He divided the children among Leah, Rachel and the two maidservants.
Gideon “divided the three hundred men into three companies (שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁים)”.
Abimelech took the people וַיֶּחֱצֵם לִשְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁים and lay in wait.

senses.definition: To divide property, a price or spoil, between parties, each taking a share; often in halves.

evidence.note: If one man's ox kills another's, “they shall sell the live ox וְחָצוּ its silver, and the dead one also יֶחֱצוּן”: each owner bears half.
“וְחָצִיתָ the spoil between those who went out to battle and all the congregation”; the result is the מֶחֱצָה of Num 31:36.
The half “which Moses divided (חָצָה) from the men who fought”.
Of Leviathan: “will partners bargain over him? יֶחֱצוּהוּ among the merchants?”

senses.definition: To live out half: men of blood “shall not halve their days”, not reach even the middle of a life.

evidence.note: “You, God, will bring them down to the pit of the grave; men of blood and deceit לֹא־יֶחֱצוּ יְמֵיהֶם; but I will trust in you.”
The same thought with the noun: “do not take me up בַּחֲצִי יָמָי”.

senses.definition: Of a flood: to come up to the neck, halving a man's height.

evidence.note: Yahweh's breath “like an overflowing torrent עַד־צַוָּאר יֶחֱצֶה”, that reaches to the neck, to sift the nations.

senses.definition: Of the Jordan struck with Elijah's cloak: to part to either side, leaving dry ground between.

evidence.note: Elijah struck the waters, “וַיֵּחָצוּ הֵנָּה וָהֵנָּה, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground”.
Elisha: “Where is Yahweh, the God of Elijah?” and the waters were divided here and there.

senses.definition: Of a people or a kingdom: to be split into separate realms.

evidence.note: “I will make them one nation in the land … one king … and they shall no longer be two nations, וְלֹא יֵחָצוּ עוֹד into two kingdoms.”
The mighty king's kingdom “shall be broken וְתֵחָץ to the four winds of the heavens”.

evidence.locator: Gen.32.8, וַיַּחַץ → διεῖλεν; Exo.21.35 → διελοῦνται; Num.31.27 → διελεῖτε; Ezk.37.22, יֵחָצוּ → διαιρεθῶσιν; διαιρέω renders חָצָה ×7

evidence.note: “He divided (διεῖλεν) to them his living”: dividing property into shares, as Exo 21:35 and Num 31:27.

opposites.note: “One nation … one king” against being divided into two kingdoms.

senses.definition: A half part: above all the half shekel of the census offering, and the half of an offering or of the spoil.

evidence.note: Each one counted gives מַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל by the shekel of the sanctuary, twenty gerahs to the shekel: “מַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל, an offering to Yahweh”.
“The rich shall not give more and the poor shall not give less than מִמַּחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל, to make atonement for your lives.”
A beka a head, half a shekel.
Half as much fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels.
The priest's grain offering, מַחֲצִיתָהּ in the morning and its half in the evening.
The half of the spoil belonging to the sons of Israel.
Zimri, commander of half the chariots.
Cities from the half tribe of Manasseh.

senses.definition: The middle of the day, midday.

evidence.note: Ezra read the law “from the light until מַחֲצִית הַיּוֹם”, from dawn to midday.

evidence.locator: Exo.30.13, מַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל → τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ διδράχμου; ἥμισυ renders מַחֲצִית ×13

evidence.note: “Does your teacher not pay the didrachma?”: the half-shekel of Exo 30:13, which the Septuagint calls “half the didrachma”.

words.summary: Three times, always of the night, in the form of an infinitive: the night's “halving”.

senses.definition: The middle of the night, the hour of the night's dividing.

evidence.note: “Thus says Yahweh: כַּחֲצֹת הַלַּיְלָה I will go out into the midst of Egypt”, fulfilled “at חֲצִי הַלַּיְלָה” (Exo 12:29).
“חֲצוֹת לַיְלָה I rise to give thanks to you for your righteous judgments.”
“In a moment they die, וַחֲצוֹת לַיְלָה the people are shaken and pass away.”

words.summary: Twice, both of the Midianite spoil that Moses divided (חָצָה) between the army and the congregation.

senses.definition: The half of a divided spoil, one party's share.

evidence.note: “הַמֶּחֱצָה, the portion (חֵלֶק) of those who went out to war”.
“מֶחֱצַת the congregation from the flock”.

words.summary: An arrow, beside the commoner חֵץ. Only about four tokens are this form (1Sa 20:36, 37 twice, 2Ki 9:24, and the written text of 1Sa 20:38); the brief's sixteen also count the plural חִצִּים of חֵץ and 1Ki 10:7 “the half”. Its cognates are those of “arrow” (Ugaritic ḥẓ, Arabic ḥaẓwa) and show ṯ̣ behind צ; how the word joins the root's “divide, half” is not yet understood.

senses.definition: An arrow shot from a bow.

evidence.note: “Run, find the arrows (הַחִצִּים) that I shoot”; and as the boy ran “he shot הַחֵצִי beyond him”.
The boy came to the place of הַחֵצִי that Jonathan had shot.
Jehu drew the bow with his full strength and struck Jehoram between the arms, “וַיֵּצֵא הַחֵצִי from his heart”.

cognates.note: Akkadian loses the ḥ and colours the vowel to e, as in other roots with ḥ; it does not show which sound stands behind צ. Cutting through, the act of dividing.

evidence.locator: armep x000097110, eṣû [slit] V (forms iṣṣi, teṣṣi; Middle Assyrian, Seleucid)
SEM001148 ḥṣy [slit] V, AKK002594 eṣû [slit] V, HEB002466 ḥaṣah [divide] V

cognates.note: Punic, the same noun as חֲצִי. Phoenician script does not show which older sounds stand behind ח and צ.

evidence.locator: SEM000147 ḥṣy [half] N, PUN000729 ḥṣy [half] N

cognates.gloss: cut off, shave off; (form III) divide a thing with another, each taking his portion; (ḥiṣṣa) portion, share
cognates.note: A geminate root ḥṣṣ, the Arabic of Hebrew חצץ, not a final-weak root; its “divide into shares” matches חָצָה “divide the spoil”. If related through a two-letter base ḥṣ, it shows ṣ behind צ, against the ṯ̣ of the arrow cognates.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 579, art. حص, حَصَّهُ (n8162)
evidence.note: “He, or it, shaved it off … He cut off from it … whence, accord. to some, the word حِصَّةٌ.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 580, art. حص, حَاصَصْتُهُ الشَّىْءَ (n8163); حِصَّةٌ (n8169)
evidence.note: “I divided with him the thing, each of us allotting to himself his portion”; “a portion, lot, or share”.

cognates.gloss: a small arrow, a cubit long, with which children play and learn to shoot; (dim.) such an arrow without a head
cognates.note: The arrow, with ẓ: ṯ̣ behind צ. The same Arabic root gives ḥuẓwa “favour, a good share”, and ḥaẓẓ is “fortune, share, lot”, which may join arrow and share through the casting of lots, but scripture does not show חֵצִי used for a lot.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 596, art. حظو, حَظْوَةٌ (n8432)
evidence.note: “A small arrow, a cubit in length, with which children play, and with which they learn to shoot … The dim. حُظَيَّةٌ signifies Such an arrow having no head.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 595, art. حظ, حَظٌّ (n8404)
evidence.note: “Fortune … and a share, portion, or lot.”

cognates.note: Ugaritic keeps ḥ apart from ḫ and writes ẓ for ṯ̣: the arrow word is ḥṯ̣.

evidence.locator: SEM000160 ḥẓ [arrow] N, UGC001959 ḥẓ [arrow] N

cognates.note: The ḥ is lost and Akkadian ṣ covers several older sounds.

evidence.locator: SEM000160 ḥẓ [arrow] N, AKK014367 ūṣu [arrow] N

cognates.note: Ge'ez ḥ (not ḫ); Ge'ez ṣ is the reflex of ṯ̣ as of ṣ.

evidence.locator: SEM000160 ḥẓ [arrow] N, GEZ002504 ḥaṣṣ [arrow] N

cognates.gloss: pluck out, tear out (the eyes); knock out (a tooth)
cognates.note: The same consonants in Syriac, but the meaning is plucking out, not dividing; Jewish Aramaic חֲצֵי (arc-chatsei) agrees. A tie to “divide” would go through cutting or splitting, which is not shown.

evidence.note: “To pluck out, tear out the eyes; to knock out a tooth … Pa. to tear or root out the eyes, the nails.”

cognates.gloss: pick out (of birds); pick one's teeth
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: the Targum of Pro 30:17 uses it for the ravens that pick out the eye that mocks a father. The same meaning as Syriac ḥṣā.

evidence.locator: s.v. חֲצֵי, citing Targ. Prov. XXX, 17; Y. Ḥall. IV, end, 60b (מִיחֲצִי שיניי, to pick my teeth with)

doctrine.statement: After Solomon the people were divided: Israel rebelled against the house of David and made Jeroboam king (1Ki 12:16–20), and even the northern kingdom split, “half of the people followed Tibni … and half followed Omri” (1Ki 16:21). Ezekiel is told to join two sticks, of Judah and of Joseph, into one in his hand (Ezk 37:16–19), and Yahweh explains it: “I will take the sons of Israel from among the nations … and bring them into their own land, and I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king shall be king over them all; they shall no longer be two nations, and no longer be divided (יֵחָצוּ) into two kingdoms” (Ezk 37:21–22). The king is named: “my servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd … they shall dwell in the land that I gave to Jacob my servant … for ever, and David my servant shall be their prince for ever” (Ezk 37:24–25). Gabriel says of Jesus, “the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob for ever” (Luk 1:32–33), and the apostles asked the risen Jesus, “will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?” (Act 1:6). From the verses: the division of the kingdom is to be undone in the land itself, on the mountains of Israel, with all the tribes gathered from the nations under one king of David's line, who is Jesus; the kingdom of God is that restored kingdom of Israel on the earth.

Zechariah sees all the nations gathered against Jerusalem to battle, the city taken, and “half of the city (חֲצִי הָעִיר) shall go out into exile” (Zec 14:2); then “Yahweh will go out and fight against those nations”, and “his feet shall stand in that day on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the Mount of Olives shall be split from its middle (מֵחֶצְיוֹ) toward the east and the west, a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall move toward the north and half toward the south … and Yahweh my God will come, and all the holy ones with you” (Zec 14:3–5). Living waters will go out from Jerusalem, half to the eastern sea and half to the western, and “Yahweh will be king over all the earth” (Zec 14:8–9). When Jesus was taken up from the Mount of Olives, the angels said, “this Jesus … will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven”, and the apostles returned to Jerusalem “from the mount called Olivet” (Act 1:9–12); Paul speaks of “the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his holy ones” (1Th 3:13). From the verses: the one who comes to stand on the Mount of Olives with his holy ones is Jesus returning as he went, after the nations' latter-day assault on Jerusalem; the mountain is split in two under his feet, and from Jerusalem he reigns over all the earth.

note: Drafted 2026-11-19. Root key חצה. Words: חֲצִי (h.ex.ac), חָצָה (h.ex.aa), מַחֲצִית (h.ex.ai), חָצוֹת (h.ex.ab), מֶחֱצָה (h.ex.ah), חֵצִי “arrow” (h.ex.ae). The name Jahzeel יַחְצְאֵל and the gentilic Jahzeelite (h.ex.af, h.ex.ag, cross-reference j.bh.ac) are in names/jahzeel.json. The cross-reference m.bo.ad (מֶחֱצָה, no tokens) is left unclaimed. חֵץ “arrow” (h.ez.ac, root חצץ) and its plural חִצִּים are left to a future חצץ entry; the brief's h.ex.ae tokens double-count them (1Sa 20:20–38, Isa 7:24, Jer 51:11, Ezk 21:26 are חִצִּים), and 1Ki 10:7 הַחֵצִי “the half” is counted under both nouns, so lexicon-support overcounts חֵצִי and slightly חֲצִי. Open questions: (1) Is חֵצִי “arrow” of this root at all? Its cognates (Ugaritic ḥẓ, Arabic ḥaẓwa) show ṯ̣ behind צ; nothing yet shows the sound behind צ in “divide, half” (Akkadian and Punic do not distinguish it), and Arabic ḥṣṣ “divide into shares”, if related, shows ṣ. If a cognate of “divide” with ṣ is confirmed, the arrow belongs with חֵץ under חצץ. Arabic ḥaẓẓ “lot, share” beside ḥaẓwa “arrow” is a lead for a link through casting lots by arrows (Ezk 21:26 shakes arrows to divine), not followed. (2) Psa 55:24 “not halve their days” and Isa 30:28 “reach to the neck” are each read from one verse. Leads not followed: Krahmalkov for Punic ḥṣy (page not checked; cited only through Anderson–Moser), DULAT for Ugaritic ḥẓ, Leslau for Ge'ez ḥaṣṣ, CAD E for eṣû. Payne Smith p. 153 for ܚܨܐ is read from OCR and should be checked against the page image. Greek: the brief counts ἥμισυ NT ×0 by lemma form; the NT has ἥμισυς (Mrk 6:23, Rev 12:14).
